A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, references, and Appendices A–B are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated figures.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements of activation norms, entropy and attention sinks, targeted MLP ablations, and downstream evaluations in Sections 3–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations on additional input distributions, component analyses, and activation-clipping experiments.

M1.justification: The Mix-Compress-Refine framework, model architectures, and proposed attention diagnostics remain unchanged. The new interventions investigate the mechanism rather than introduce a revised model or learning/inference procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds evaluations on The Stack, FineWeb, and MATH (v2 Figures 9–11). These introduce source-code inputs and broaden the prose and mathematical input distributions used to test synchronized compression, sinks, and activation norms, while retaining the original coverage.

E2.justification: v2 Figures 15–16 add the weaker, alignment-free bounds as explicit empirical comparators to the full bounds; v1 Figures 12–13 plotted only the full bounds against measurements. The downstream LogitLens and TunedLens comparison methods remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The stated Pythia 410M MLP-ablation layers change from 5–7 to 0 and 5–7. v2 also introduces an activation-clipping sweep with gamma values 100, 10, 0.5, and 0.1, and reports 5K-example evaluations for the added datasets. These are focused additions to the evaluation design.

E4.justification: v2 adds attention-versus-MLP contributions to BOS norm, clipping-strength sensitivity, and empirical checks without the alignment term (Appendix B.1, Figures 15–20). Together with the additional input-distribution checks, these substantially expand testing of the proposed mechanism beyond v1's targeted MLP removals.

E5.justification: Appendix B.3 newly discloses fixed seed 123 for linear probing. Existing mean/standard-deviation reporting and Fisher-z aggregation remain unchanged; the disclosure does not establish additional repeated runs or new uncertainty-estimation procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds results for the three input datasets, weaker bounds, component contributions, and clipping sensitivity. It also replaces the Qwen and Pythia ablation curves (v1 Figure 14; v2 Figures 17–18). Pythia shows stronger but incomplete sink suppression under a changed intervention, not a same-setting improvement. Downstream performance plots are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 explicitly states the weaker alignment-free bounds, including p1 >= c/(c+1), and the corresponding dominance and entropy specializations. v1 only mentioned the possibility of weaker bounds. The main theorem, corollaries, and all Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims linking massive activations to compression and sinks, proposing three computational phases, and explaining task-dependent optimal depths. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explanation of LLaMA-3-8B's problematic layerwise correlations and discusses less predictable sink responses under clipping. It removes the explicit Pythia exception from Section 3.3 and the original ablation discussion, although Appendix B still acknowledges model-dependent exceptions.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies PyTorch-default Adam settings and no weight decay for linear probes, and clarifies that GSM8K questions and answers are concatenated into prompts. These improve documentation without establishing changes to the existing probe training or data preparation.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for MATH, The Stack, FineWeb, and Adam. The related-work discussion and positioning of the unified mechanism relative to prior research otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section structure are retained. Changes include a shortened proof sketch, localized appendix explanations, a correlation footnote, the conference header, and removal of the Meta FAIR affiliation.

P2.justification: v2 substantially revises the empirical displays: it adds dataset and mechanism figures, separates the ablation plots and adds norm panels, and overlays weaker bounds. It also merges the existing Pythia 6.9B checkpoint plot into Figure 2 and moves the existing norm-equalization figure into the main text; these moves do not constitute new results.

improvement.justification: The broader distribution checks and additional mechanism analyses strengthen empirical support, while the probe details improve reproducibility. The gain is limited by weaker visibility of the Pythia exception and an erroneous Figure 20 caption: it says increased compression, whereas the curves and accompanying prose show increased entropy.
